title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 132 (Constitution of National Financial Reporting Authority)

content.overview: The Central Government may, by notification, constitute a National Financial Reporting Authority to provide for matters relating to accounting and auditing standards under this Act. NFRA recommends accounting and auditing standards, monitors and enforces compliance, oversees the quality of service of the professions associated with ensuring compliance, and investigates professional or other misconduct of members or firms of chartered accountants registered under the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949.
content.glance: NFRA recommends accounting and auditing standards, monitors compliance, and investigates professional misconduct of auditors of prescribed classes.
content.study:
## Section 132 — National Financial Reporting Authority

**Constitution.** Central Government may constitute NFRA by notification.

**Functions.** Recommend accounting and auditing policies and standards to the Central Government; monitor and enforce compliance; oversee quality of service of the professions associated with ensuring compliance; perform other functions in the section.

**Investigation.** Power to investigate professional or other misconduct of a member or firm of chartered accountants and to impose the penalty and debarment the section states.

**Standards notification.** NFRA recommends; the Central Government notifies standards under section 133.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.
